title: Never import `@content` (or content/source) from src/scripts/**, never import `three` statically, and never import three/examples/jsm or three/addons
body: src/scripts/** is the only code bundled for the browser. 1) `@content` resolves to content/source/index.ts -> json-source.ts, which statically imports zod and both datasets: one import ships them to every visitor. Types cross only through src/scripts/lab/types.ts (no runtime imports); build-time helpers belong in src/lib/ (see lab-data.ts). 2) `three` (~127 KB gzip) has exactly ONE importer, src/scripts/lab/graph-3d.ts, and boot.ts loads it with `await import("./graph-3d")`. A single static import of graph-3d (or of three) from any module makes Rollup hoist it into the critical chunk, even if other imports are dynamic. 3) `three/examples/jsm/*` and `three/addons` are forbidden on behaviour, not weight: OrbitControls registers a `wheel` listener with preventDefault, i.e. scroll hijacking. Write the control by hand (interaction.ts does). All three are caught only after `pnpm run build` by `pnpm run test:bundle` (looks for ZodObject/dataset strings and WebGLRenderer in critical chunks), so get it right while editing.
not_derivable: The checks only fire after a full build; an agent writing a new client module sees no local hint unless it happens to read types.ts or graph-3d.ts headers.

evidence.summary: Header: imports nothing at runtime; @content would drag zod + dataset; static graph-3d import hoists three.
Header: the only file importing three; OrbitControls rejected because it registers wheel with preventDefault.
Asserts no WebGLRenderer in critical chunks (line ~139) and no zod/dataset in any bundle (lines ~183-194).
